Light Up a Life is coming round again, and the tree will be in the window at Magdalen Street.

Several of you have asked on the page whether we'd be doing the tree this year. We are. Memory tags are on the counter from Monday 16 November, with a suggested donation of £3. If you'd rather write your tag at home, there are envelopes on the counter for that too, and you can bring it in whenever suits you.

Seven years ago this month, my husband Ray died at the hospice. It doesn't feel like seven years, and it does. The first year I hung his tag, I could hardly write his name. My hand simply wouldn't do it. Now I write it at the counter, with the same pen, and I find it's a small comfort to have that little ritual each November.

The tree is for anyone who is grieving, not only families who have been cared for at the hospice. If you've lost someone, whatever the circumstances, you're welcome to write a name and hang it. And if you'd just like to come in and stand by the tree for a minute, please do. You don't need to buy anything or say anything. Plenty of people do exactly that, and it's as much a part of the tree as the tags are.

The tree goes into the window on the Saturday before the lights come on, and we switch them on on Saturday 28 November at 4pm. The Gildencroft Primary choir are coming back to sing three or four carols for us, and Doreen has promised her mince pies again. I'd suggest arriving a little early for those.

Every name on a tag will be read out at the hospice remembrance service on Sunday 13 December at 3pm, in the day centre. You don't have to come to the service for your person's name to be read, but anyone who would like to come is very welcome. The lights stay on in the window until Twelfth Night.

Thank you to everyone who wrote a name last year. The tree carried 412 names, and every one of them matters to someone. Thank you for coming in, for trusting us with those names, and for letting us remember alongside you.

Jean
